1.explanation:
• audits/uses-rel-preconnect-test.js: Contains the unit tests for the preconnect audit. Examining this will show how the audit discovers existing <link rel=preconnect> tags and what cases it currently treats as “missing”.
• audits/uses-rel-preload-test.js: The preload audit uses very similar DOM-parsing logic. Comparing its tests will help pinpoint how it handles deduplication or origin matching differently.
• audits/network-requests-test.js: The preconnect audit operates over the set of networkRequests. Reviewing this test confirms how origins are collected and normalized before hints are checked.
• gather/html-without-javascript-test.js: This gatherer pulls all <link> elements from the DOM (including rel=preconnect/dns-prefetch). Inspecting it reveals how link tags and their hrefs are captured for use by the audit.
• computed/network-records-to-devtools-log.js: Converts raw network records into the DevTools protocol format that underpins how the audit correlates requests with hint origins. Investigating this will help you simulate and reproduce the issue in tests.
• config/default-config-test.js: Shows how the “uses-rel-preconnect” audit is wired into the Performance > Opportunities category. Useful to confirm you’re running the correct audit and to adjust thresholds or grouping for your repro setup.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse against a page that already includes <link rel="preconnect"> hints for third-party origins, the “Avoid multiple, costly round trips to any origin” opportunity still flags those same origins. In the screenshot you can see links for “https://www.google-analytics.com” and “https://fonts.gstatic.com” are already present in the DOM, yet Lighthouse recommends adding preconnect/dns-prefetch for two origins (“google-analytics.com” and “fonts.googleapis.com”). The audit doesn’t dedupe or match existing hints, resulting in a false positive.
